pronunciation.approximation: Say "illapa" with the stress and length implied by the scholarly restoration "Illapa".
pronunciation.note: The ASCII form "illapa" is a DNS compromise; the restoration "Illapa" preserves the name's scholarly dignity.

domains.title: Illapa
domains.subtitle: Thunder
domains.lead: Illapa is thunder, lightning, war. The name means "Thunder" and belongs to the incan tradition.

cards.name: Sacred Name
cards.desc: The restoration Illapa returns the figure to scholarly recognition.

cards.name: Living Tradition
cards.desc: Honored in incan myth, cult, and cultural memory.

symbols.name: Name
symbols.meaning: The restored form Illapa, carrying scholarly and cultural weight.

mythology.lead: The stories of Illapa place thunder, lightning, war at the center of a living mythological world.

myths.title: Origins
myths.text: Illapa appears in incan tradition as thunder, lightning, war. The name's meaning, "Thunder", shapes the narratives told about this figure.

myths.title: Worship and Memory
myths.text: Devotees and later tradition-keepers preserved Illapa in ritual, text, and iconography, ensuring the name survived into the modern scholarly record.

lore.culturalLegacy: Illapa remains a touchstone for understanding incan religion, art, and identity.
scholarlySources: Bauer, Brian S., The Sacred Landscape of the Inca (1998).
